question.prompt: The length of a rectangle is increased by \(10\%\) and the width is decreased by \(10\%.\) What percent of the old area is the new area?

solutions.explanation:
The new length is \(110\%\) of the old length, and the new width is \(90\%\) of the old width. Let the original positive length and width be \(L\) and \(W\). Since a rectangle's area is length times width, its new area is
\[
(1.10L)(0.90W)=0.99LW.
\]
The old area is \(LW\), so the new area is \(\boxed{99\%}\) of the old area, choice B.
solutions.title: Multiply the percentage factors
